destination.name: Southern Highlands
destination.tagline: Cool-climate villages and gardens in the hills southwest of Sydney.
destination.description: The Southern Highlands is a run of country towns and villages about 80 minutes by car from Sydney, popular for weekends away. Bowral has Corbett Gardens and the cricket museum attached to Bradman Oval, Berrima is a Georgian sandstone village with a courthouse and district museum, and Mount Gibraltar above Mittagong is an extinct volcano with a rim walk. It is cooler than Sydney and has more distinct seasons, with leaves falling in autumn.

goodToKnow.title: Drive from Sydney
goodToKnow.detail: Allow about 80 minutes to Bowral; weekday and Friday afternoons add 30 to 45 minutes. Trains run on the Southern Highlands Line, but most services end at Campbelltown.

goodToKnow.title: Bradman Museum hours
goodToKnow.detail: The cricket museum on St Jude Street, Bowral is open 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM, and a walking tour from it passes sites linked to Don Bradman.

goodToKnow.title: Cycling Mittagong to Bowral
goodToKnow.detail: Bowral and Moss Vale are linked by a riverside cycleway, but Mittagong to Bowral is harder: the four-lane road past Mount Gibraltar is the only route that avoids going over it.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} suit the highlands: leaves fall in autumn, spring is cooler than Sydney, and the gardens are in flower.
